Bundled third-party code

Snice ships the following vendored dependencies. Their licenses apply to their respective portions:

  • Heroicons (MIT) — embedded SVG glyphs used as built-in default icons. © Tailwind Labs. github.com/tailwindlabs/heroicons
  • PDF.js (Apache 2.0) — vendored in components/pdf-viewer/ for the PDF viewer component. © Mozilla. mozilla.github.io/pdf.js
  • pica-route (MIT) — runtime route matcher.
  • tslib (0BSD) — TypeScript runtime helpers (peer dependency).

Inspiration & acknowledgments

Snice didn't appear in a vacuum. These projects shaped its design, API, or aesthetic:

  • Lit — the canonical web-component runtime. Snice's render pipeline is not Lit, but the lifecycle patterns share ancestry with Lit Element.
  • Shoelace — proved a comprehensive web-component UI kit could actually work at scale.
  • Tailwind CSS — the HSL color scale (50–950) we use for color primitives, and the overall token naming discipline.
  • Radix UI — accessibility patterns, especially around keyboard nav and focus management.
  • shadcn/ui — inspiration for the "copy the code into your app" philosophy, and for token conventions like --primary/--muted.
  • Linear & Vercel — aesthetic references for the dark theme and minimal aesthetic direction.
  • Material Design (M3) — reference for density, elevation, and the "on-color" text-over-fill pattern.
  • Atlassian Design System & Shopify Polaris — prior art for the document components (invoice, estimate, work order, receipt).
  • D3 & Tableau — color palette choices for the data-vis accent scale.
  • Heroicons, Lucide, Phosphor — icon design direction.
  • Packery — algorithm reference for the grid-packing layout used in snice-binpack.

If you see something that should be credited here and isn't, please open an issue.
